transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I guess I'm here because flying has started to feel, well, way scarier than it probably should. 

It's a bit embarrassing to admit, but just the idea of getting on a plane makes me picture that bad turbulence from my honeymoon flight again. I mean, I know people fly safely every single day, so I know I shouldn't be making a big deal out of it. I really hope I'm not wasting your time with something so silly... is it okay that I came in to talk about this?
Is your anxiety mainly focused on flying, or do you also experience similar worries in other situations, like driving, being in crowded places, or even just thinking about leaving home?

No, no, it's really just the flying. I mean, driving is totally fine, and I love going out, being around people... leaving the house isn't an issue at all. I'm actually a pretty normal, functional person most of the time, I promise! It's just... when it comes to getting on an airplane, that's where I get a little, um, stuck. I hope that makes sense? I know it probably sounds a bit strange to just have this one specific thing that bothers me so much.
When you think about flying, does it get to the point where you actively avoid it, like turning down trips or opportunities to travel?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I *actively* avoid it, exactly. I mean, I still try to be reasonable about things. But... lately, I have found myself, you know, suggesting we just drive instead of fly for vacations, even if it takes a lot longer. And there was a work training recently that I... well, I kind of found an excuse not to go to, just because the flight felt a bit too overwhelming right now. 

And, honestly, even just sitting down to plan a trip or talk about booking tickets... I get so worked up that I usually have to ask my husband to sit right there with me, just so I don't completely lose my nerve and cancel the whole idea. I know that probably sounds incredibly needy of me, relying on him just to talk about a trip. I'm really trying to be better about it, though! Is it... is it normal to need that kind of support for something like this?
When you think about flying or start planning a flight, do you ever feel sudden, intense physical symptoms like your heart racing, feeling dizzy, short of breath, or like you're losing control?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I completely lose control or anything dramatic like that. I really try to keep it together! But... I guess I do get a little bit of a physical reaction, yeah. 

Like, if I'm just looking at flights on my laptop for a work conference, or... honestly, even if I'm just outside and hear a plane flying overhead, my chest does get a little tight right away. And I get this... this sudden rush of panic, I suppose you could call it. It's just this strong feeling like I need to immediately shut my laptop or just get away from whatever is making me think about it. 

But I always try to calm myself down right after! I know it's silly to let a sound or a website make my chest tight. Does... does that sound like the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm explaining it right.

Do you find that these physical reactions and feelings of panic happen mostly when you're actually thinking about an upcoming flight, or do they also happen in other situations when you're not directly anticipating flying?

Well, um... no, it's really just tied to the flying. I mean, I don't just sit around having panic attacks for no reason! I'm actually a very calm person normally, I swear. 

It's really only when I'm, you know, faced with something related to airplanes. Like if I have to book a ticket, or if a trip is coming up and I start thinking about being on the plane... or like I said, if one flies right over me and catches me off guard. If I'm not dealing with anything flight-related, I'm completely fine. I don't have those chest-tightening moments at the grocery store or anything like that. 

I hope that's a good thing? Like, it means I'm mostly okay, right?
Has this fear of flying been present for a long time, or did it start more recently after that honeymoon flight you mentioned?

Well, um... no, it hasn't been a lifelong thing or anything like that. I used to be completely fine with airplanes! I promise I wasn't always this much of a worrywart about it. 

It really just started right after that turbulent flight back from my honeymoon. That was... gosh, about two years and five months ago now. I know it probably sounds a bit silly that I'm still letting one bumpy ride affect me over two years later. I really am trying to get past it, I just haven't quite figured out how yet. 

Is it... is it okay that it's lasted that long from just one bad experience? I hope I don't sound completely ridiculous holding onto it for two and a half years.
Has your fear of flying caused you any significant distress or affected your ability to function in your job, relationships, or other important areas of your life?

Well, um... I really try not to let it affect things too much! I'm still doing great at my job, and I manage everything at home just fine. I promise I'm not falling apart or anything like that. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it has gotten in the way a little bit. Nothing major! Just... well, my supervisor has suggested a few trainings and conferences that would be really good for my career, and I've... I've sort of been finding excuses to pass on them because they involve flying. I know I shouldn't do that, and I always feel a bit guilty about it. 

And, um, on a personal level... I've been really excited to go to Florence for a long time, but I keep pushing the trip back because I just can't bring myself to book the flight. 

So I guess it is causing a little bit of trouble, but I'm really trying to work on it! I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm not taking my career or my life seriously. Does... does that make sense?
How long does the anxiety or discomfort typically last once you've been exposed to something related to flying, like booking a flight or hearing a plane overhead?

Well, um... it really doesn't last very long at all, I promise! I'm usually pretty quick to bounce back. 

If I hear a plane or see one, you know, it's just a quick flutter in my chest, and then I tell myself it's fine and I move on. It might take a few minutes for my heart to settle completely, but I don't let it ruin my whole day or anything. And with booking... well, I just get a little worked up while I'm thinking about it, but once I step away from the computer, I'm usually back to normal pretty quickly. 

I really try not to dwell on it, you know? I just take a deep breath and keep going. That's a good way to handle it, right? I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than I should be.
Have you ever had a sudden surge of panic or physical symptoms like chest tightness when you weren't thinking about flying or being near an airplane?

Oh, no, no, definitely not! I promise I don't just panic out of nowhere. 

If I'm just going about my day, you know, working at the preschool or running errands, I'm completely fine. I don't get those chest tightness feelings or anything like that unless it's specifically about... well, about airplanes. 

I'm actually a very calm person normally! I really don't want you to think I'm just anxious all the time about everything. It's really just this one little thing with the flying. That's... that's normal for this kind of thing, right? To just have it be about the one specific fear?
When you experience these physical symptoms like chest tightness or a rush of panic related to flying, do they ever peak within a few minutes and feel like a full panic attack, even if short-lived?

Oh, um, a full panic attack? No, no, I wouldn't call it that at all! I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is. 

It's just... you know, a little rush, a bit of tightness, like we talked about. It doesn't get out of control or peak into anything huge or scary. I just feel a little uncomfortable for a minute, and then I brush it off and keep going. I'm really good at keeping it together, I promise! 

I don't think I've ever had a real panic attack. That sounds really intense, and I'm definitely not dealing with anything that severe. I'm just a little nervous about the planes, that's all. I'm answering these questions okay, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

When you start thinking about an upcoming flight in the days or hours before actually boarding, do you feel increasing anxiety or worry about it ahead of time, or does the anxiety only really hit when you're actually at the airport or on the plane?

Um, honestly, I don't really get that big build-up of worry beforehand. I promise I'm not the type to just sit around stressing for days! If I know I have a trip coming up, I just focus on my work with the kids at the preschool and keep myself busy. I'm pretty good at just putting it out of my mind, you know? 

It really only hits me when I'm actually right there, like walking into the airport or getting ready to board. And even then, it's just that quick little flutter we talked about. I definitely don't spend the whole week before agonizing over it or anything like that. 

That's... that's a good sign, right? I hope that means I'm doing pretty well with all of this!

When you know you're going to be flying in the next day or two, do you find yourself getting more anxious or worried about it as the time gets closer, or does the anxiety still only really happen when you're at the airport or stepping onto the plane?

Oh, um, yeah, I think it's... well, like I was just saying, it really is just when I get to the airport. I don't get worked up the day or two before at all. I'm sorry if I didn't explain that clearly a second ago! 

But yes, I promise I'm not sitting at home worrying as the flight gets closer. I just keep busy with my schedule and the preschool. The nerves really only start when I'm actually looking at the plane or stepping onto it. I'm pretty good at keeping it out of my head until the very last second. 

I hope I'm making sense! Am I answering that right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
When you're not actively booking a flight, hearing a plane, or at the airport, do you ever find yourself worrying or thinking about flying in the future and feeling anxious about it?

Oh, no, definitely not! I really don't sit around worrying about it if I don't have a reason to. I mean, if I'm not traveling or... or right there near an airport, it barely even crosses my mind. 

I'm usually just so focused on the kids at the preschool and, you know, getting through my daily routine. I'm definitely not one of those people who just stews over things that aren't even happening yet. I really try to stay positive and focused on the present. 

That's normal, right? I mean, I think that shows I'm handling it pretty well, wouldn't you say? I just really want to make sure I'm doing the right things here.
When you see pictures of airplanes, watch scenes of flying in movies, or even just imagine being on a plane, do you feel anxious or get those physical symptoms like chest tightness?

Um, well, I guess... maybe a little bit? I mean, I really try not to let it bother me, but if I'm, say, looking up flights for a work conference or something, or even if I just hear a loud plane flying right overhead, I do get this... this quick little tightness in my chest. 

It's just a tiny rush of panic, you know? Like I just want to shut my laptop or push the thought away real quick. But I don't let it ruin my day or anything! I just take a breath and move on. 

Is that... is that okay to admit? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm completely falling apart over a picture or a sound. I really am trying my best to manage it!

Um, well, I guess... maybe a little bit? I mean, I really try not to let it bother me, but if I'm, say, looking up flights for a work conference or something, or even if I just hear a loud plane flying right overhead, I do get this... this quick little tightness in my chest. 

It's just a tiny rush of panic, you know? Like I just want to shut my laptop or push the thought away real quick. But I don't let it ruin my day or anything! I just take a breath and move on. 

Is that... is that okay to admit? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm completely falling apart over a picture or a sound. I really am trying my best to manage it!

inference.note: This turn added F40.22 (Specific phobia, situation type) as the patient's fear is specifically tied to flying, triggered by a specific event (turbulence on honeymoon), and causes avoidance and distress limited to that context. The patient's symptoms are not consistent with panic disorder (F41.0) or agoraphobia (F40.00), as anxiety is not present in other situations, nor does it generalize beyond the specific fear cue.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a specific phobia (aviophobia) triggered by exposure to flight-related stimuli, with symptoms of anticipatory anxiety, avoidance behavior, and physical reactivity limited exclusively to the context of flying or thinking about flying. There is no evidence of panic attacks or generalized anxiety, which would support F40.20 (other phobias).
